description: Next.js App Router pages are caller-reachable render roots, not API handlers. Four real page.tsx files with resolved default component exports become rendered-page entries while the route.ts handler remains the sole http-route; the fourth also proves that parallel slots and interception markers are filesystem instructions, not URL text. The negatives hold each over-reporting boundary: layout.tsx wraps addresses but creates none, a named export does not satisfy Next's page contract, a literal default export is not a component, and pages/dashboard.tsx belongs to the older Pages Router and is not a server entry merely because it renders React. The one finding proves that destructured searchParams are caller input even though this frontend has no aggregate parameter value for that binding.

expected.note: the rendered page is a remote entry even though it is counted apart from the API, and Next fills the destructured searchParams binding from its URL
